ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: Rurikid princes ruled the first great East Slavic state from Kiev, a federation of principalities on the river route from the Baltic to Byzantium, until the Mongols sacked Kiev in 1240.
In 988 Vladimir the Great accepted Christianity from Byzantium and married the emperor's sister Anna, bringing churches, Church Slavonic writing and Byzantine art to Kievan Rus'.
This merchant city-state of the Russian north elected its officials and archbishop, hired princes by contract and traded furs with the Hanseatic League until Ivan III annexed it in 1478.
Batu Khan's conquest of 1237–1240 destroyed Ryazan, Vladimir and many other cities, and the Rus' principalities then paid tribute to the Golden Horde for some two centuries.
A small appanage on the Moskva River grew rich collecting tribute for the Golden Horde, ended Tatar overlordship at the Ugra River in 1480 and annexed Novgorod and Tver.
Founded when Ivan IV was crowned the first Tsar of All Russia in 1547, the Tsardom conquered the Volga khanates and crossed Siberia to the Pacific.
Proclaimed emperor in 1721 after victory over Sweden, Peter reorganised the army, built a navy, founded St Petersburg and subordinated the Church to the state.
Grown to some 22.8 million square kilometres from the Baltic to the Pacific, the empire freed some 23 million serfs in 1861 by Alexander II's Emancipation Edict.
The February Revolution of 1917 forced Nicholas II to abdicate, and in the October Revolution the Bolsheviks under Lenin seized power, then won the civil war that followed.
Founded in 1922 as the first communist state, it industrialised under Stalin at enormous human cost, rivalled the United States as a superpower and was dissolved in 1991.
